title: Limiting Use of Section 409 of Penal Code to Professional Agents
what_it_is: Limiting Use of Section 409 of Penal Code to Professional Agents

sections.label: Section 409 sentences and Government steps
sections.summary: 12 persons serve sentences under section 409, convicted before the High Court changed the interpretation, and the Public Prosecutor intends no applications for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether there are any persons convicted under section 409 of the Penal Code who are currently serving imprisonment sentences based on the interpretation of the law as it existed before the decision of the Court of Appeal of 1 February 2018 limiting the use of the said provision to professional agents; and (b) if so, what steps will the Government take in respect of the sentences of these persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There are now 12 persons serving sentences for offences under section 409 of the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They were convicted and sentenced before the High Court reviewed and changed the interpretation of the law regarding section 409.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Public Prosecutor does not intend to file any applications in respect of them.

sections.label: Three of 12 are public servants
sections.summary: Of the 12 persons, three are public servants.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, if you look at these 12, three of them are public servants.

sections.label: Court interpretations do not affect them
sections.summary: The High Court and Court of Appeal interpretations do not affect them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The High Court and Court of Appeal's interpretations do not affect them.

sections.label: City Harvest Home Detention policy
sections.summary: A policy cleared with AGC means those convicted in the City Harvest case will not qualify for Home Detention if applied by the Commissioner of Prisons.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As for the City Harvest case, we looked at the principles that are applicable and we took advice from AGC as to whether, under the law, they would be entitled to community-based programmes, which will include Home Detention.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have now a policy and, if that policy is applied by the Commissioner of Prisons, those convicted in the City Harvest case will not qualify for Home Detention.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is something to be decided by the Commissioner of Prisons.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But if the policy is applied, and that policy has been cleared with AGC, then they will not qualify.
